session_summary: Phase 9c: Delivered vessel panel polish (In Transit/Parked labels, labelled dock fields), always-on NextDeparture overlay with off-hours messaging, landmark removal, and dock popup clarity improvements. 73/73 tests green. Water taxi AIS research concluded: not feasible via AIS — Toronto Harbour water taxis are legally exempt from AIS carriage under Transport Canada's sheltered waters classification.

agent_feedback.worked_well: T1 (VesselCard) and T2 (NextDeparture) completed cleanly in one pass each — precise file-scoped task descriptions prevented scope creep.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: T3 (landmark removal + dock popup) hit max_turns=25 without committing. The task combined file deletion, JSX changes across two components, and CSS additions — slightly too large for 25 turns.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: For tasks combining a deletion + multi-file edits, either raise max_turns to 35 or split into two tasks: (a) delete file + FerryMap import removal, (b) dock popup label + DockSummary component.

agent_feedback.worked_well: All 4 gates green on first run with no fixes needed. Added API URL integrity check proactively — good initiative.

overall_notes: Recurring issue: Docker agent commits push to remote before host can push, requiring a merge step each time. Should document this as standard workflow in scrum-master: after Docker agent session, always do git pull --no-rebase -X ours before git push. Water taxi research via general-purpose Agent tool worked well for a non-code research task despite scrum-master normally using run_agent_in_docker — the Agent tool is appropriate for pure research that requires WebSearch/WebFetch.
